1.text: I swear by the Day of Resurrection

2.text: And I swear by the reproaching soul<sup foot_note="228127">1</sup> [to the certainty of resurrection].

footnotes.228127: - i.e., that of the believer, which blames him when he falls into sin or error.

3.text: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?

4.text: Yes. [We are] Able [even] to proportion his fingertips.

5.text: But man desires to continue in sin.<sup foot_note="228128">1</sup>

footnotes.228128: - Literally, "to sin ahead of him."  This refers to the disbeliever, who denies the Day of Account.

6.text: He asks, "When is the Day of Resurrection?"

9.text: And the sun and the moon are joined,

10.text: Man will say on that Day, "Where is the [place of] escape?"

12.text: To your Lord, that Day, is the [place of] permanence.

13.text: Man will be informed that Day of what he sent ahead<sup foot_note="228129">1</sup> and kept back.<sup foot_note="228130">2</sup>

footnotes.228129: i.e., his deeds, which await him in the Hereafter.
footnotes.228130: i.e., that which he did not do or which he delayed.

14.text: Rather, man, against himself, will be a witness,<sup foot_note="228131">1</sup>

15.text: Even if he presents his excuses.

16.text: Move not your tongue with it, [O Muḥammad], to hasten with it [i.e., recitation of the Qur’ān].

17.text: Indeed, upon Us is its collection [in your heart] and [to make possible] its recitation.

18.text: So when We have recited it [through Gabriel], then follow its recitation.

19.text: Then upon Us is its clarification [to you].

20.text: No! But you [i.e., mankind] love the immediate

22.text: [Some] faces, that Day, will be radiant,

footnotes.228132: - The people of Paradise will actually see their Creator in the Hereafter.

24.text: And [some] faces, that Day, will be contorted,

25.text: Expecting that there will be done to them [something] backbreaking.

26.text: No! When it [i.e., the soul] has reached the collar bones<sup foot_note="228133">1</sup>

footnotes.228133: - At the time it is about to leave the body when one is on the verge of death.

27.text: And it is said, "Who will cure [him]?"

28.text: And he [i.e., the dying one] is certain that it is the [time of] separation

29.text: And the leg is wound about the leg,<sup foot_note="228134">1</sup>

footnotes.228134: - From the difficulties the person faces at death or his sudden awareness of the realities of both this world and the Hereafter.  It may also refer to his shrouding after death.

30.text: To your Lord, that Day, will be the procession.<sup foot_note="228135">1</sup>

footnotes.228135: - Literally, "driving" or "herding" or "the place to which one is driven."

31.text: And he [i.e., the disbeliever] had not believed, nor had he prayed.

32.text: But [instead], he denied and turned away.

33.text: And then he went to his people, swaggering [in pride].

35.text: Then woe to you, and woe!

36.text: Does man think that he will be left neglected?<sup foot_note="228136">1</sup>

footnotes.228136: - i.e., to no end, without responsibility, or without being returned to the Creator for judgement.

37.text: Had he not been a sperm from semen emitted?

38.text: Then he was a clinging clot, and [Allāh] created [his form] and proportioned [him]

39.text: And made of him two mates, the male and the female.

40.text: Is not that [Creator] Able to give life to the dead?
